use_when.text: Use it in the Back Office when an action changes a record and is hard to undo, such as approving a claim.
Use Danger when the action removes or rejects something.
Write the title as a question that names the action, and the confirm button as the same action.
Keep the body to one or two sentences on what happens next.
Show it over a dimmed page with color/bg/scrim behind it.

dont_use_when.text: Do not use it for information that needs no decision. Use Callout.
Do not stack dialog boxes on top of each other.
Do not use vague labels such as OK or Yes.
Do not put a long form inside it.
Do not recolour it outside the bound tokens.

best_practice.text: Put the safe choice, Cancel, on the left and the confirm action on the right.
Let Escape close it, the same as Cancel.

variant_intent.intent: Use Default for actions that change a record without removing or rejecting it.
Use Danger when the action removes or rejects something.

placement.text: In the Back Office, over a dimmed page.

pairs_with.how: Actions row: Outline Cancel, then Primary confirm
Nested Callout between body and actions, Privacy by default, off with Show callout
The story opens it from an Outline "Open dialog" Button, which gets focus back on close

a11y.text: Renders role="dialog", or role="alertdialog" when Type is Danger, with aria-modal="true".

aria-labelledby points at the

title and aria-describedby at the body

.
On open, focus moves to Cancel; focus is kept inside while open; on close or unmount, focus returns to the element that had it before.
Tab and Shift+Tab wrap between the first and last focusable element.
Cancel comes before Confirm in the DOM, so it is first in the reading order.
A press on the scrim does nothing and does not move focus out of the dialog.
Rendered through a portal at the end of <body>.
Use role="dialog" (or "alertdialog" for Danger) with aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing at the title.
Move focus into the dialog box when it opens, keep it inside, and return it to the trigger when it closes.
Close it with Escape, the same as Cancel.
Put Cancel first in the reading order so the safe choice comes first.
Title, body and button text are above 4.5:1. The red confirm label is 5.8:1 in Light and 4.5:1 in Dark.
